releases.notes:
- Installing from a URL or QR asks how: Install, Save and install, Save, install and delete, or Save; the top screen explains each one.
- Google Drive share links work: NSA fetches the file itself, under its own name.
- Saving a download writes it in order, so the SD card keeps up: steady speeds on big files, on New 3DS and 2DS alike.
- Downloads open a new connection only when it is clearly faster (at most four), and drop one if the speed collapses.
- A link that leads to a web page instead of a file says so, instead of saving or installing the page.

- Saving from a URL and sending to another 3DS use only the connections that make it faster, found as they go: often faster than before, and the console keeps answering meanwhile.
- Sending to another 3DS needs this version on both consoles.
- Save backups show Checkpoint's and NSA's badges instead of "[Checkpoint]" and "[NSA]".

- Downloads from Dropbox links work, to save and to install (they failed with "Forbidden").
- Saving a big file from a URL is faster: it comes in long pieces, opening only the connections that help, so the FTP and the web page keep answering meanwhile.
- One transfer at a time: a second one (FTP, web page, download, another 3DS) is told so at once instead of slowing both; the web page shows what is transferring.
- FTP and downloads a little faster.
- Send whole folders to another 3DS, and choose to keep the original path when receiving.
- Deleting asks in red; going up a folder selects the one you came from.
- Sending to another 3DS shows a steady speed: it no longer jumps between 0 and twice the real one.

- Faster downloads: big files come over 8 connections on every model, servers such as catbox.moe split too, and a stalled piece is asked for again; the install screen says how many connections.
- Installing from a URL or a QR code can now Save the CIA in /nsa/received/ instead, to install it later.
- FTP and web page transfers about twice as fast, and turning the FTP server off no longer freezes NSA.
- Settings -> "Pause music for FTP" (on by default on an Old 3DS, where transfers go 10-25% faster without it); the top bar shows the FTP server at work and the web server running.
- Titles opens much faster (names, icons and product codes are kept between runs), and System opens a list of details: console, network, SD card and battery.
- Rows that open another screen show an arrow.

- Faster downloads: big files come over 8 connections on every model, servers such as catbox.moe now split too, and a stalled piece is asked for again; the install screen says how many connections.
- FTP and web page transfers about twice as fast, and turning the FTP server off no longer freezes NSA.
- Settings -> "Pause music for FTP" (on by default on an Old 3DS, where transfers go 10-25% faster without it); the top bar shows the FTP server at work and the web server running.
- Titles opens much faster: names, icons and product codes are kept between runs.
- System opens a list of details: console, network, SD card and battery.
- Rows that open another screen show an arrow.

- Saves: export, import and send the save data, extra data and SpotPass data of a title to another 3DS, with a list of every backup (NSA's and Checkpoint's) to restore, send or delete.
- A web page to manage the console from a computer's browser (Settings -> Web server, with a PIN): files, titles with icons, saves, installing from URLs, and the console's screens live with its buttons.
- Background music made by the console itself (Lift, Calm and Shop, on by default), with volume sliders for sounds and music, and draggable scrollbars.
- A banner jingle of NSA's own, and a fix for the Old 2DS crashing when closing the app with HOME.

- The FTP server is now on by default and only serves the SD card's files. Driving the console from a computer (screenshots, key presses and touches, and installing a CIA with SITE INSTALL) works only while the file sdmc:/nsa/remote.flag exists on the SD card.
- Updating NSA over FTP needs that file too; delete it to turn remote use off again. Builds made for development keep it always on.
- A new README with pictures of every part of NSA, taken on a real console.

- New themes: Pixel (a pixel font, square corners, bars in blocks) and HOME (big icon tiles, dialogs as a sheet from the bottom), and a Yellow accent colour.
- Files: view pictures (3D photos too), read and edit text files, play MP3, WAV, FLAC and Ogg music, cut and move, previews and icons by file type, and run a .3dsx from the list.
- Faster downloads (several connections at once) and a history in Remote install to install again.
- Interface sounds, a new NSA icon and banner, and Advanced and the delete warnings drawn in a soft red.

- NSA installs as its own app next to FBI, keeps its data in sdmc:/nsa/ and updates itself from the Stable or Beta channel.
- New look: themes, accent colours, night mode, English and Spanish, 3D on the top screen; Titles, Files, Tickets and Extra data redone with pictures, filters, search and sorting.
- Send a file or an installed title to another 3DS over the Wi-Fi (four connections at once), or with no router at all; a cut transfer goes on where it stopped.
- The receiver installs a CIA at once or saves it in a folder it picks. Export as CIA makes a CIA of an installed title (installing it needs Luma3DS).
- Grouped main menu, a System page, touch feedback, smooth scrolling and dragging in lists.
- Every send and receive is logged in sdmc:/nsa/transfer-log.txt.
